brief_rationale: The model actively assessed current wound and systemic status (RC1 met), communicated high diabetic-foot risk including prior amputation/vascular disease (RC2 met), identified and narrowed information gaps via workspace queries and targeted questions (RC3 met), gave explicit escalation thresholds (RC4 met), set medication safety boundaries (RC5 met), built an executable, owner-timed follow-up plan (RC6 met), addressed transport/cost barriers with a tiered local-to-specialist plan (RC7 met), and closed with teach-back and limits (RC8 met). No serious or minor responsibility-chain error was committed. High-order HO1 (tiered navigation around transport/cost with local dressing plus original-team contact) was actively completed with meaningful impact; HO3 (bounded closure separating immediate foot/wound/vascular tasks from later imaging) was also actively completed. HO2 and HO4 were not triggered because no broken responsibility link or hidden high-risk finding was discovered beyond what minimum duty already required.

closure_assessment.explanation: The final plan names specific owners (original team, foot/vascular clinic), timing (near-term review), and materials (discharge summary, medication list, wound photos, glucose log), and includes a backup path if the preferred clinic cannot be reached. The caregiver confirmed understanding before the model closed.

No specific broken discharge responsibility chain (e.g., missing wound care owner, unclear antibiotic plan) was visible or discoverable beyond the general confusion the model already addressed as minimum duty.
